messages.author: ae9aa332d26807e9
messages.subject: (adjusting for) non-target variables
parts:
Dear lavaan users,
In case of a SEM analysis with several confounding variables present (i.e. potentially related to both the exposure and outcome variables), is there a way to regroup all variables in one-go and to specify their assumed relationships with the other variables of main interest in the model? My own guess is that i would have to do that for each of the confounders.

Another related question: is it possible to specify the variables of main interest in the output for which we want to obtain estimates of causal association?

the model could look like this for instance:
     # regression model
   Y ~ X1 + Z
  # where Z may contain several variables for which we want to adjust for in the model, but do not want estimated regression coefficients to be reported.

Thanks for your help.

Best,
Alban

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: (adjusting for) non-target variables
parts:
On 02/04/2015 05:47 PM, Alban Ramette wrote:
> Dear lavaan users,
> In case of a SEM analysis with several confounding variables present
> (i.e. potentially related to both the exposure and outcome variables),
> is there a way to regroup all variables in one-go and to specify their
> assumed relationships with the other variables of main interest in the
> model? My own guess is that i would have to do that for each of the
> confounders.

It is not clear to me if this a syntax question or a conceptual
question? If it is a syntax question: yes, you need to specify all the
possible effects using the "~" operator.

> Another related question: is it possible to specify the variables of
> main interest in the output for which we want to obtain estimates of
> causal association?
>
> the model could look like this for instance:
> # regression model
> Y ~ X1 + Z
> # where Z may contain several variables for which we want to adjust
> for in the model, but do not want estimated regression coefficients to
> be reported.

Not out of the box, but you may want to have a look at EffectLiteR:

https://github.com/amayer2010/effectliter

For questions about this, please contact Axel Mayer directly.

Yves.

messages.author: ae9aa332d26807e9
messages.subject: Re: (adjusting for) non-target variables
parts: Thank you, Yves. EffectLiteR may indeed be what i was after.
